title: The goal status strip reads a multi-node build: N of M criteria covered, and what is waiting on what
description:
SPIDR child 4 of parent task-4423d2a4c3084d579c132b253d36b502 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-04). dependsOn child 2 task-1d7b9df2579c491992b55de791c99f4f: the strip's new sentence names the `depends:` blocking state that child 2 introduces.

This is the surviving half of the parent's UI paragraph. MOST OF THAT PARAGRAPH IS ALREADY BUILT - re-measured at HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb. Do NOT rebuild any of it:
- THE BOARD ALREADY SHOWS EVERY NODE ACROSS SIX COLUMNS. `apps/control-room/src/v2/board/board-columns.ts:20` `BOARD_COLUMNS = ["QUEUED","WORKING","REVIEW","REWORK","DONE","BLOCKED"]`; line 73 already renders a QUEUED node's build order as `after ${node.dependsOn.join(", ")}`; `board-lanes.tsx:77` already shows a "Depends on" field.
- `/runs/read` ALREADY EMITS dependsOn per node: `apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts:98-104` derives it from `graph.content.snapshot.edges`, and `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.ts:62,222,230` already decodes it.
- READY-TO-CLOSE IS ALREADY GATED ON 100% COVERAGE: `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-status.ts:139-143` requires `progress.verified === progress.criteria` with a readable contract before it returns READY_TO_CLOSE, and `progress {criteria, verified}` (line 107-108) already comes from the `POST /documents/coverage/read` totals.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING, measured:
- The strip does not say the COVERAGE FRACTION in operator words while a goal is mid-build. `deriveGoalStatus` (goal-status.ts:89, 164 lines total) carries `progress` but the BUILDING/executing stage sentence does not spend it, so an operator watching a 3-node goal sees no "N of M" until it is finished.
- No stage words for the new multi-node reality: nothing distinguishes "3 nodes, 1 accepted, 2 queued behind it" from "1 node building". The `depends:` token child 2 adds has no strip-level sentence.
- The parent's description also asks for a "Needs-you: Approve expansion" entry. THAT IS OUT OF SCOPE by owner ruling comment-fbe64776 ("The expansion kinds are OUT of this row"): with the fence lifted the human approves the WHOLE graph in ONE existing plan-approval decision, so no new Needs-you entry is needed. Do not add one.

FILES: `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-status.ts` (164 ln) and `goal-status-strip.tsx` (108 ln) plus their tests (`goal-status.test.tsx`); touch `board-columns.ts` only if its QUEUED sentence needs the blocking node's title rather than its key.
definitionOfDone: The goal status strip states the coverage fraction in operator words whenever the goal is executing and the coverage read is available - e.g. "2 of 7 acceptance criteria verified" - sourced from the existing `progress {criteria, verified}` in goal-status.ts, not recomputed. A test asserts the exact rendered sentence for (verified 2, criteria 7) and for (verified 0, criteria 7).

The strip distinguishes a multi-node build from a single-node one: when nodes are queued behind an unfinished dependency the sentence names how many are waiting and on what. A test drives a 3-node goal with a->b->c, a accepted, and asserts the rendered sentence names the waiting count and the blocking node.

READY_TO_CLOSE still fires ONLY at 100%: a regression test asserts (verified 6, criteria 7) does NOT reach READY_TO_CLOSE and (verified 7, criteria 7) does. Assert the stage value, not merely the words.

The zero-coverage and unreadable-contract paths are unchanged and asserted: coverage absent or contract unreadable renders the existing sentence, with no NaN, no "undefined", and no "0 of 0" - assert the literal output for a null progress.

No new Needs-you entry, no new offer kind, no new daemon route: `git diff --stat` for this row touches only apps/control-room paths. (Owner ruling comment-fbe64776 put the expansion kinds out of scope; the whole graph is approved by the one existing plan-approval decision.)
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: BROWSER-ONLY ROW. If a needed fact is missing from the daemon's existing reads, say so in a step note and render what IS available - do not add a daemon route here; that is a different row's 8-touchpoint work.
The board (PR #23) and /runs/read already carry dependsOn end to end. Reuse those values; a second derivation of build order in the strip is how the board and the strip come to disagree.

Words are the product here (memory ui-legibility-pass-landed-2026-09-04): write for a human operator, not for a test. Avoid an aria-live region that announces on every poll - PR #26's review caught exactly that; announce once and keep the counter outside the live region.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited from the parent): no security-boundary or policy work.

implementationPlan.description: IMPLEMENT THE FOLD AND SPEND IT. apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-status.ts (164 lines): (a) `agentsOf` (:71-80) gains a count of nodes blocked on an unmet dependency, folded by testing each BLOCKED step's `missing` for the `depends:` PREFIX — prefix, not exact match, because the token carries a variable nodeKey (the same shape `labelForMissing` reads in work-labels.ts). Leave `blocked` and `replanned` exactly as they are: they key on the `escalation` and `replan` tokens and are different questions. (b) The WORKING branch (:150-158) spends it: when nodes are waiting on build order, say so and name the blocking node rather than reporting them as unclaimed. Keep the existing sentence for the case where nothing is waiting — this step ADDS a reading, it does not rewrite the branch. implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 — IMPLEMENT THE FOLD AND SPEND IT. goal-status.ts 184 -> 223 lines (under the 250 target). Step 2's three arms go GREEN: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 12 passed (12)`, exit 0.

(a) THE FOLD. New `blockersOf(step)` (:84-90) returns the node keys a BLOCKED step is held behind: `missing.filter(t => t.startsWith(DEPENDS_TOKEN_PREFIX)).map(slice).filter(k => k.length > 0)`. PREFIX, not exact match — the token carries a variable nodeKey, so an exact match is a permanent zero (the mutation step 5 drills). The prefix is IMPORTED from `./work-labels.js`, not re-spelled: work-labels.ts:127 already owns `DEPENDS_TOKEN_PREFIX = "depends:"` and `labelForMissing` reads the same shape, so there is exactly one spelling of the token in the control-room and a rename cannot desynchronise them.

`agentsOf` gains TWO keys and changes nothing else:
  waiting: steps.filter(step => blockersOf(step).length > 0).length   — NODES held, so a node behind two parents counts ONCE
  waitingOn: Object.freeze([...new Set(steps.flatMap(blockersOf))])   — DISTINCT blockers, so two nodes behind one parent name it once
`accepted`, `blocked`, `replanned`, `total` and `working` are byte-identical: `blocked` still keys on the exact "escalation" token and `replanned` on "replan". They are different questions and the ESCALATION stage's Needs-you anchor still routes to a decision that exists.

(b) SPENDING IT. The WORKING branch's inline ternary became `workingDetail(agents)` (:113-125), a named function, because the sentence now has three cases and an inline nested ternary would be unreadable. It ADDS a reading, it does not rewrite the branch:
  - every node accepted -> the existing "Every node is accepted; ..." sentence, verbatim
  - nothing waiting     -> the existing "{n} node(s) is/are claimed right now. Nothing needs you until a review is exhausted." verbatim (goal-status.test.tsx:109 asserts it and stayed green untouched)
  - waiting > 0         -> the queued clause LEADS: "2 nodes are waiting for n1 and n2 to be accepted first; 0 nodes are claimed right now. Nothing needs you until a review is exhausted."
The claimed clause is reused, not duplicated — it is lowercased into the second position by `claimed[0]?.toLowerCase() ?? ""` + slice(1), so the two readings can never drift apart. `nodeWords` (:107-111) joins blockers as "n1" / "n1 and n2" / "n1, n2 and n3".

The `remaining` local was removed from `deriveGoalStatus` (its only reader moved into `workingDetail`, which recomputes `total - accepted`); no behaviour change, and leaving it would have been an unused binding under noUnusedLocals.

NO NEW GoalStage, as the plan required: a node waiting on build order is still WORKING. STAGE_WORDS and every consumer of the union are untouched, and `stage: "WORKING"` is asserted in the step-2 arms so a later widening cannot slip in silently.

PAUSE FORK RESPECTED (this was not in the plan's line numbers — a peer landed ProviderPause after the row was written): the WORKING branch is `paused !== null ? pausedNext(paused) : {...}`, and `workingDetail` sits in the NON-paused arm only. A paused goal's one thing to do is still to wait for the reset; step 4 adds the regression arm for that.

FILE SIZE: 223 physical lines. All four functions well under 50 lines (largest is `deriveGoalStatus`, unchanged in size). No `any`, no non-null assertions — `keys[keys.length - 1] ?? ""` and `claimed[0]?.` satisfy noUncheckedIndexedAccess without asserting.

(a) DoD 3 — READY_TO_CLOSE ONLY AT 100%, four assertions, all on the `stage` VALUE not the words:

  Then the same pair with TWO nodes queued behind build order: (7,6) -> `{agents:{waiting:2}, stage:"WORKING"}` and (7,7) -> `{agents:{waiting:2}, stage:"READY_TO_CLOSE"}`. That second pair is the one that matters here: it pins that the new fold perturbs the completion gate from NEITHER side. Coverage decides closability, the board does not — a goal can be 100% verified with nodes still queued, and that pre-existing precedence is now asserted rather than assumed. Needed the fixture's new `criteria` param; before this the denominator was hard-wired to 4 and the 6/7 case was unwritable.

(b) DoD 4 — NULL AND ZERO PATHS, all three branches, literal output asserted:

(c) NO NODE STEPS: empty step list -> `{agents:null, progress:{criteria:4,verified:2}, stage:"UNKNOWN"}`. Plus a step that IS a node.deliver and IS BLOCKED on `depends:x` but belongs to ANOTHER goal's node key -> `agents` still null. That second half guards the scoping seam: the surface is project-wide, and a fold that counted every `depends:` token on the frame would report a foreign goal's queue on this strip.

(d) PAUSE PRECEDENCE (not in the plan — the WORKING branch grew a `paused` fork after this row was written): two nodes queued AND the provider paused -> `{agents:{waiting:2}, stage:"WORKING"}` with the pause's own label and detail, unchanged. The waiting sentence lives in the non-paused arm only; while the seat is rate-limited the one thing to wait on is still the reset, not build order.

=== ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FINDINGS, both FIXED (goal-status.ts 223 -> 235 lines) ===
(1) UNREADABLE SENTENCE AT SCALE. `nodeWords` recited EVERY distinct blocker, so a wide graph produced "9 nodes are waiting for p0, p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6, p7 and p8 to be accepted first; ...". That is the row's own failure mode — a sentence nobody finishes tells an operator nothing. Now bounded: `NAMED_BLOCKERS = 3`, then a count — "p0, p1, p2 and 2 more". 1, 2 and 3 blockers are unchanged ("n1" / "n1 and n2" / "n2, n3 and n4"), so no arm written before the fix moved. New arm "summarises a wide graph rather than reciting every blocking node key" pins it, and per global rail 1 it ASSERTS THE CASE WAS BUILT (`{total:6, waiting:5, waitingOn:["p0".."p4"]}`) before asserting the sentence — a sweep that silently yielded fewer blockers would otherwise pass.
(2) THE TWO COUNTS COULD DISAGREE. `waiting` and `waitingOn` each folded `blockersOf` independently (`steps.filter(s => blockersOf(s).length > 0)` vs `steps.flatMap(blockersOf)`), so a later edit to one predicate could ship a count with no names, or names with a zero count — and `nodeWords([])` would then render "0 nodes are waiting for  to be accepted first". Now ONE pass: `const blockers = steps.map(blockersOf)`, with `waiting` filtering it and `waitingOn` flattening it. The invariant "waiting > 0 implies at least one nameable blocker" is now structural, not a coincidence of two predicates agreeing.

Checklist items considered and NOT changed: pure function, no IO, no shared state, no retry path, so the concurrency and side-effect sections are N/A. Nulls/empties are covered by step 4(b). A `depends:` naming a node OUTSIDE this goal's contract is rendered verbatim — deliberate: the daemon said it, and the board never renames a node.
